Man Buys 2026 Lexus LC 500 Convertible Inspiration Series for $120K, Adds 761 Miles, Sells for $147
31 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Since this is America and everybody loves Lexus, it's no wonder that this barely-driven, limited edition LC 500 Convertible just sold at auction for roughly $27,000 over MSRP. While the seller didn't present a sticker, we know the MSRP on one of these babies came down to around $120,000 or so. So yeah, there's a quick $27k for you. Flipper heaven.
Despite the limited-edition factor, which is always highly desirable among collectors (and buyers in general), the LC500's calling card is still its 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8 engine - one of the last naturally aspirated V8s available in a luxury grand tourer. It's not particularly powerful by modern standards, but it does offer that immediate throttle response and linear power curve that enthusiasts crave. Not to mention an incredible soundtrack as you approach 7,300 rpm.
Then there's the Toyota/Lexus reliability factor. Or reputation, I should say. This particular V8 engine is exceptionally reliable, and so is the LC 500, for something this expensive. As for the Inspiration Series spec, it's a swan song for the LC 500 , whose production is set to end in 2026 with no immediate direct replacement announced.
Let's take a closer look at what makes this particular car special, starting with the Wind colorway. It's very elegant and it works well together with the LC 500's design language. Other visual highlights include the convertible soft-top, triple-beam LED headlights, the flush door handles, a surround-view camera, front canards, a rear diffuser, PPF on the front fascia, plus a set of 21" forged wheels with Michelin rubber and Lexus-branded calipers.
Meanwhile, inside is where you'll find the white and Saddle Tan leather upholstery, heated, ventilated, and power-adjustable front sport seats, a color-coordinated center console, dashboard, and door panels, a head-up display, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, a Mark Levinson sound system, ambient lighting, automatic climate control, a heated steering wheel, and a center console plaque that identifies this car as #165 of 550 Inspiration Series models produced.
Photo: Bring a Trailer In terms of electronic driver aids, there's the Pre-Collision System, Dynamic Radar Cruise Control, Intuitive Parking Assist, a blind-spot monitor, rear cross traffic alert, and lane-keep assist.
As for that previously-mentioned 5.0-liter V8 engine , it's pushing 471 horsepower and 398 lb-ft (540 Nm) of torque to the rear wheels via a 10-speed automatic gearbox and a Torsen limited-slip rear differential. In a straight line, the LC 500 can get you from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in just 4.5 seconds. More than quick enough, I'd say.
So, what do you guys think, is $147,000 (plus a buyer's fee) too much for an LC 500? Or is the Inspiration Series totally worth it? Me personally, I can understand the valuation, but I also don't see these going up in value again any time soon. I think I'd just rather have a regular LC 500 Convertible.
